records.literal_gloss: In year three of [the] reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon [to] Jerusalem and besieged it.

en.L: In the third year of the kingship of Jehoiakim king of Judah, came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon [to] Jerusalem and besieged it.
en.B: In the third year of Jehoiakim's reign as king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
en.R: When Jehoiakim had been king of Judah for three years, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem. His army surrounded the city and attacked it.

pt.L: No terceiro ano do reinado de Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, veio Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, [a] Jerusalém e a sitiou.
pt.B: No terceiro ano do reinado de Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, veio a Jerusalém e cercou a cidade.
pt.R: Fazia três anos que Jeoaquim era rei de Judá quando Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, chegou a Jerusalém. O exército dele cercou a cidade e a atacou.

fr.L: La troisième année du règne de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, vint Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, [à] Jérusalem, et il l’assiégea.
fr.B: La troisième année du règne de Joïaqim, roi de Juda, Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, vint à Jérusalem et l’assiégea.
fr.R: Joïaqim était roi de Juda depuis trois ans quand Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, est venu à Jérusalem. Son armée a encerclé la ville et l’a attaquée.

es.L: En el año tercero del reinado de Joacim, rey de Judá, vino Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, [a] Jerusalén y la sitió.
es.B: En el tercer año del reinado de Joacim, rey de Judá, Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, llegó a Jerusalén y la sitió.
es.R: Cuando Joacim llevaba tres años como rey de Judá, Nabucodonosor, el rey de Babilonia, llegó a Jerusalén. Su ejército rodeó la ciudad y la atacó.

ko.L: 유다 왕 여호야김의 통치 제3년에 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 예루살렘[에] 와서 그곳을 포위했다.
ko.B: 유다 왕 여호야김이 다스린 지 3년째 되는 해에 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에 와서 그 성을 포위했다.
ko.R: 여호야김이 유다 왕이 된 지 3년째 되는 해에 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 예루살렘에 왔다. 그의 군대는 그 성을 에워싸고 공격했다.

vi.L: Vào năm thứ ba của vương quyền Giê-hô-gia-kim vua Giu-đa, Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đến Giê-ru-sa-lem và vây hãm nó.
vi.B: Vào năm thứ ba triều vua Giê-hô-gia-kim nước Giu-đa, Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn kéo đến Giê-ru-sa-lem và vây hãm thành.
vi.R: Khi Giê-hô-gia-kim làm vua Giu-đa được ba năm, thì Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn kéo đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Quân đội của ông bao vây thành và tấn công.

sw.L: Katika mwaka wa tatu wa utawala wa Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda, alikuja Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli Yerusalemu, akauzingira.
sw.B: Katika mwaka wa tatu wa utawala wa Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda, Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuja Yerusalemu, akauzingira mji huo.
sw.R: Yehoyakimu alipokuwa amekuwa mfalme wa Yuda kwa miaka mitatu, Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuja Yerusalemu. Jeshi lake liliuzunguka mji na kuushambulia.

decisions.choice: the third year of Jehoiakim: about 605 BC
alternatives: the third year by the reckoning of Jeremiah, that is, about 606 BC
a date that joins the campaign of 605 BC with the siege of 597 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiakim ruled Judah from about 609 to 598 BC (2 Kings 23:36). Jeremiah dates Nebuchadnezzar's first year to Jehoiakim's fourth (Jeremiah 25:1; 46:2), the year Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish, 605 BC. Daniel's "third year" is usually explained by a different way of counting a king's years: in the Babylonian way, the months before a king's first new year were not counted as a year of his reign, so Jehoiakim's third year by that count is the fourth by Jeremiah's. Kings and Chronicles say that Nebuchadnezzar came up against Jehoiakim and that some of the temple's vessels were taken to Babylon (2 Kings 24:1; 2 Chronicles 36:6-7), but no other source tells of a siege of Jerusalem in 605 BC, and some think the verse joins that campaign to the later siege of 597 BC. The book does not settle how its dates match other records.

decisions.choice: Daniel among the Writings: where the book stands in the Hebrew Bible
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew Bible, Daniel stands among the Writings (with Psalms, Job, Esther, Ezra and the rest), not among the Prophets. The Greek and Latin Bibles placed it after Ezekiel, among the prophets, and Jesus calls Daniel a prophet (Matthew 24:15). Its first six chapters tell stories of Daniel and his friends at the courts of foreign kings; its last six give Daniel's visions. Part of the book (2:4-7:28) is written in Aramaic, not Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon: Nebuchadnezzar II, who ruled from 605 to 562 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar was crown prince when he beat the Egyptian army at Carchemish in 605 BC, and became king the same year when his father Nabopolassar died. He took Jerusalem in 597 BC and destroyed it in 587 BC (2 Kings 24-25). The spelling of his name here follows the Hebrew of this book; Jeremiah also uses the form Nebuchadrezzar, which is closer to the Babylonian.

decisions.choice: His army surrounded the city and attacked it
decisions.reason: "Besieged" is a word many young readers will not know, so Readable says what a siege is: an army surrounding a city to take it. Readable also starts with how long Jehoiakim had been king, which is what "the third year of the reign" means.

decisions.choice: Jeoaquim; Nabucodonosor; a Babilônia
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the kings keep the forms 2 Kings and Jeremiah give them in Portuguese, "Jeoaquim" and "Nabucodonosor", the usual Brazilian spelling of the name as Daniel spells it (m3); Jeremiah's "Nabucodorosor" is kept for the spelling with r, which Daniel does not use.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced and in the passé composé at Readable, imparfait for repeated action, for Daniel 1-6; speech keeps the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As the French style guide and the term sheet for these books ask: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense of plain modern French for new readers. Daniel's own first-person narrative from chapter 7 follows the same split.

decisions.choice: "Nabuchodonosor" at every level, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The usual French form, used in published Kings and Jeremiah; Daniel's names follow the published books.

decisions.choice: "Joacim"; "Nabucodonosor"
decisions.reason: The published Spanish forms (2 Kings 24). Daniel spells the Babylonian king with -n-, so he is "Nabucodonosor" throughout the book; Ezekiel's -r- form is "Nabucodorosor"

decisions.choice: The dated heading follows the Kings formula: "통치 제3년에" (L); "다스린 지 3년째 되는 해에" (B); "유다 왕이 된 지 3년째 되는 해에" (R), with the year in figures
decisions.reason: Years are written in figures and the regnal formula is worded as in the published Kings, Chronicles and Jeremiah, so dated headings read alike across the books.

decisions.choice: The narration of Daniel is in the plain written style in 했다; God takes the honorific -시- and 께서 at every level, kings and people do not (느부갓네살이 … 왔다)
decisions.reason: The speech levels set for the narrative books and the prophets hold in Daniel; the Aramaic chapters (2:4b-7:28) are narrated the same way.

decisions.choice: Giê-hô-gia-kim, Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa, Ba-by-lôn
decisions.reason: The published forms of Kings, Chronicles and Jeremiah. Daniel keeps the Protestant transliterations of the Vietnamese style guide for every name in the book: Đa-ni-ên, Bên-xát-sa, Đa-ri-út người Mê-đi, Si-ru.

decisions.choice: "Nebukadneza" for Nebuchadnezzar at every level, and "Nebukadreza" wherever a verse has the r form
decisions.reason: The published Swahili of 2 Kings 24-25 and 2 Chronicles 36 spells the king "Nebukadneza"; each verse keeps the form its Hebrew or Aramaic uses, as in Jeremiah. Book-wide choice for Daniel.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י בְּיָד֜וֹ אֶת־יְהוֹיָקִ֣ים מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה וּמִקְצָת֙ כְּלֵ֣י בֵית־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיְבִיאֵ֥ם אֶֽרֶץ־שִׁנְעָ֖ר בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהָ֑יו וְאֶת־הַכֵּלִ֣ים הֵבִ֔יא בֵּ֖ית אוֹצַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave [the] Lord into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah and some of [the] vessels of [the] house of God, and he brought them [to the] land of Shinar [to the] house of his god, and the vessels he brought [to the] treasure house of his god.

en.L: And [the] Lord gave into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah and part of the vessels of the house of God; and he brought them [to the] land of Shinar, [to the] house of his god; and the vessels he brought into the treasure house of his god.
en.B: The Lord handed Jehoiakim king of Judah over to him, along with some of the vessels from the house of God. He carried them off to the land of Shinar, to the temple of his god, and put the vessels in the treasury of his god.
en.R: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar defeat Jehoiakim king of Judah. The Lord also let him take some of the cups and bowls from God's temple. Nebuchadnezzar took them to the land of Babylonia, to the temple of his own god. He put them in the storehouse of his god's temple.

pt.L: E o Senhor entregou na mão dele Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, e parte dos utensílios da casa de Deus; e ele os levou [para] a terra de Sinear, [para] a casa do seu deus; e os utensílios ele levou para dentro da casa do tesouro do seu deus.
pt.B: O Senhor entregou nas mãos dele Jeoaquim, rei de Judá, junto com alguns dos utensílios da casa de Deus. Ele os levou para a terra de Sinear, para o templo do seu deus, e pôs os utensílios no tesouro do seu deus.
pt.R: O Senhor deixou que Nabucodonosor vencesse Jeoaquim, rei de Judá. O Senhor também deixou que ele levasse alguns dos copos e das tigelas do templo de Deus. Nabucodonosor os levou para a terra da Babilônia, para o templo do seu próprio deus. Ele os guardou no depósito do templo do seu deus.

fr.L: Et le Seigneur livra en sa main Joïaqim, roi de Juda, et une partie des ustensiles de la maison de Dieu ; et il les emporta [au] pays de Shinéar, [à] la maison de son dieu ; et les ustensiles, il les fit entrer dans la maison du trésor de son dieu.
fr.B: Le Seigneur lui livra Joïaqim, roi de Juda, ainsi qu’une partie des ustensiles de la maison de Dieu. Il les emporta au pays de Shinéar, dans le temple de son dieu, et déposa les ustensiles dans le trésor de son dieu.
fr.R: Le Seigneur a permis à Nabuchodonosor de vaincre Joïaqim, roi de Juda. Le Seigneur l’a aussi laissé prendre une partie des coupes et des bols du temple de Dieu. Nabuchodonosor les a emportés au pays de Babylonie, dans le temple de son propre dieu. Il les a mis dans la salle du trésor du temple de son dieu.

es.L: Y el Señor entregó en su mano a Joacim, rey de Judá, y parte de los utensilios de la casa de Dios; y los llevó [a la] tierra de Sinar, [a la] casa de su dios; y los utensilios los metió en la casa del tesoro de su dios.
es.B: El Señor le entregó a Joacim, rey de Judá, junto con algunos de los utensilios de la casa de Dios. Nabucodonosor se los llevó a la tierra de Sinar, al templo de su dios, y puso los utensilios en el tesoro de su dios.
es.R: El Señor permitió que Nabucodonosor venciera a Joacim, rey de Judá. También permitió que se llevara algunas de las copas y tazones del templo de Dios. Nabucodonosor los llevó a la tierra de Babilonia, al templo de su propio dios, y los guardó en el depósito del templo de ese dios.

ko.L: 그리고 주님께서 유다 왕 여호야김과 하나님의 집의 그릇들 가운데 일부를 그의 손에 넘겨주셨다. 그리고 그는 그것들을 시날 땅 그의 신의 집[으로] 가져갔고, 그 그릇들은 그의 신의 보물 창고에 들여놓았다.
ko.B: 주님께서 유다 왕 여호야김을 그의 손에 넘겨주시고, 하나님의 집에 있던 그릇들 가운데 일부도 넘겨주셨다. 그는 그것들을 시날 땅에 있는 자기 신의 신전으로 가져가서, 그 그릇들을 자기 신의 보물 창고에 넣어 두었다.
ko.R: 주님께서는 느부갓네살이 유다 왕 여호야김을 이기게 하셨다. 또 주님께서는 그가 하나님의 성전에서 잔과 대접 같은 그릇들을 얼마쯤 가져가게 하셨다. 느부갓네살은 그것들을 바빌로니아 땅에 있는 자기 신의 신전으로 가져갔다. 그리고 그 그릇들을 자기 신전의 창고에 넣어 두었다.

vi.L: Và Chúa đã phó vào tay ông Giê-hô-gia-kim vua Giu-đa cùng một phần các vật dụng của nhà Đức Chúa Trời; và ông mang chúng đến xứ Si-nê-a, [vào] nhà của thần mình; và các vật dụng ấy ông đem vào kho báu của thần mình.
vi.B: Chúa phó Giê-hô-gia-kim vua Giu-đa vào tay ông, cùng với một số vật dụng trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời. Ông mang chúng về xứ Si-nê-a, vào đền thờ của thần mình, và cất các vật dụng ấy vào kho báu của thần mình.
vi.R: Chúa để cho Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa đánh bại Giê-hô-gia-kim vua Giu-đa. Chúa cũng để cho ông lấy đi một số chén bát và đồ dùng trong đền thờ của Đức Chúa Trời. Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa mang chúng về xứ Ba-by-lôn, vào đền thờ của thần ông, và cất chúng vào kho của đền thờ ấy.

sw.L: Na Bwana akatia mkononi mwake Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda na sehemu ya vyombo vya nyumba ya Mungu; naye akavipeleka nchi ya Shinari, [kwenye] nyumba ya mungu wake; na vyombo hivyo akaviingiza katika nyumba ya hazina ya mungu wake.
sw.B: Bwana akamtia Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda mikononi mwake, pamoja na baadhi ya vyombo vya nyumba ya Mungu. Naye akavichukua mpaka nchi ya Shinari, kwenye hekalu la mungu wake, akaviweka vyombo hivyo katika nyumba ya hazina ya mungu wake.
sw.R: Bwana alimruhusu Nebukadneza amshinde Yehoyakimu mfalme wa Yuda. Bwana alimruhusu pia achukue baadhi ya vikombe na mabakuli kutoka hekalu la Mungu. Nebukadneza alivipeleka katika nchi ya Babeli, kwenye hekalu la mungu wake mwenyewe. Akaviweka katika ghala la hekalu la mungu wake.

decisions.choice: the Lord gave Jehoiakim into his hand: the defeat was God's doing, not only Nebuchadnezzar's
decisions.reason: The book's first sentence about God says that the Lord, not the Babylonian king, decided the outcome. The same verb returns in verses 9 and 17: God "gave" Daniel favor and "gave" the young men knowledge. The whole book turns on this: the God of Israel rules over the kingdoms of the world (2:21; 4:14). The title used here is *'adonai*, "the Lord", not the divine name.

decisions.choice: the vessels of the house of God: the cups, bowls and other objects of the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: These are the sacred objects of the temple's service. They return in the story of Belshazzar's feast, where they are used for drinking (5:2-4), and Cyrus later sends them back to Jerusalem (Ezra 1:7-11). 2 Chronicles 36:7 also says that Nebuchadnezzar put temple vessels in his temple in Babylon.

decisions.choice: the land of Shinar: Babylonia
decisions.reason: Shinar is an old name for the land of Babylon, the plain where the tower of Babel was built (Genesis 11:2; Isaiah 11:11; Zechariah 5:11). Using it here may also recall that story of human pride against God.

decisions.choice: he brought them to the house of his god: the vessels, perhaps with the captives
decisions.reason: The word "them" most likely means the vessels, which the end of the verse names again. Some read it as Jehoiakim and the vessels together, but the verse goes on to say only where the vessels were put. The god is probably Marduk, chief god of Babylon, also called Bel (see 4:5).

decisions.choice: let Nebuchadnezzar defeat ... take ... Nebuchadnezzar took
decisions.reason: Readable names Nebuchadnezzar for "him" and "he", says "cups and bowls" for "vessels", and "Babylonia" for Shinar (m3). It splits the long sentence into four.

decisions.choice: os utensílios (L, B); Sinear
decisions.reason: "Utensílios" is the Portuguese word for the cups, bowls and other objects of the temple's service (m2); "vasos" now suggests flowerpots or vases. The old name for Babylonia is spelled "Sinear", as Genesis 11:2 has it in Portuguese; Readable says "a Babilônia", as the English says "Babylonia" (m3).

decisions.choice: "ustensiles" for the vessels of the house of God (Literal, Balanced); "des coupes et des bols" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Ustensiles" is the word the published French uses for the temple's vessels in Kings; "vases" would suggest flower vases. Readable names the objects, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "la tierra de Sinar" (L, B); "la tierra de Babilonia" (R)
decisions.reason: "Sinar" is the published form (Genesis 11:2); R names the region, as the English R does

decisions.choice: "주님" for Adonai, with the honorific ("넘겨주셨다")
decisions.reason: Adonai is the title "Lord", not the name YHWH, so it is "주님" and never the divine_name span, as the term sheet sets for Daniel.

decisions.choice: "시날 땅" (L, B); "바빌로니아 땅" (R)
decisions.reason: Shinar is spelled as in Genesis 10:10; Readable names the region, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Chúa, in ordinary letters and with no span
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here is Adonai ("Lord"), not the divine name, so it is "Chúa", never the capitals "CHÚA" that stand for YHWH. Daniel uses the divine name only in chapter 9.

decisions.choice: xứ Ba-by-lôn (R); xứ Si-nê-a (L, B)
decisions.reason: Shinar is the old name for Babylonia (Genesis 10:10 "xứ Si-nê-a"); Readable names the country the reader knows, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the object marker "-vi-" (the vessels): "akavipeleka" (L), "akavichukua" (B), "alivipeleka" (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili must give "them" a noun class. The vessels are the nearer and main object; the reading that the captives went too stays in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְאַשְׁפְּנַ֖ז רַ֣ב סָרִיסָ֑יו לְהָבִ֞יא מִבְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וּמִזֶּ֥רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֖ה וּמִן־הַֽפַּרְתְּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Ashpenaz, chief of his eunuchs, to bring from [the] sons of Israel, and from [the] seed of the kingship, and from the nobles,

en.L: And the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the sons of Israel, both of the royal family and of the nobles,
en.B: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, his chief court officer, to bring in some of the Israelites from the royal family and from the nobility,
en.R: The king gave an order to Ashpenaz, the chief of his palace officials. He told him to choose some young men from among the people of Israel who had been brought to Babylon. They were to be from the king's family and from the important families.

pt.L: E o rei disse a Aspenaz, o chefe dos seus eunucos, que trouxesse [alguns] dos filhos de Israel, tanto da descendência real como dos nobres,
pt.B: Então o rei ordenou a Aspenaz, o chefe dos funcionários da sua corte, que trouxesse alguns dos israelitas da família real e da nobreza,
pt.R: O rei deu uma ordem a Aspenaz, o chefe dos oficiais do seu palácio. Mandou que ele escolhesse alguns jovens do povo de Israel que tinham sido levados para a Babilônia. Eles deviam ser da família do rei e das famílias importantes.

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Ashpenaz, le chef de ses eunuques, d’amener [quelques-uns] des fils d’Israël, de la descendance royale et des nobles,
fr.B: Puis le roi ordonna à Ashpenaz, le chef de ses hauts fonctionnaires, de faire venir des Israélites de la famille royale et de la noblesse,
fr.R: Le roi a donné un ordre à Ashpenaz, le chef de ses fonctionnaires du palais. Il lui a dit de choisir quelques jeunes hommes parmi le peuple d’Israël qui avaient été emmenés à Babylone. Ils devaient venir de la famille du roi et des familles importantes.

es.L: Y dijo el rey a Aspenaz, el jefe de sus eunucos, que trajera de los hijos de Israel, tanto del linaje real como de los nobles,
es.B: Entonces el rey ordenó a Aspenaz, jefe de los funcionarios de su corte, que trajera a algunos israelitas de la familia real y de la nobleza,
es.R: El rey le dio una orden a Aspenaz, el jefe de los funcionarios del palacio. Le dijo que escogiera a algunos jóvenes del pueblo de Israel que habían sido traídos a Babilonia. Debían ser de la familia del rey y de las familias importantes.

ko.L: 그리고 왕이 그의 내시장 아스부나스에게 이스라엘 자손 가운데서, 곧 왕족과 귀족들 가운데서 [몇 사람을] 데려오라고 말했다.
ko.B: 그때 왕은 궁중 관리장 아스부나스에게 명령하여, 이스라엘 사람들 가운데서 왕족과 귀족 집안의 사람들을 데려오게 했다.
ko.R: 왕은 왕궁 관리들의 우두머리인 아스부나스에게 명령을 내렸다. 바빌론에 끌려온 이스라엘 사람들 가운데서 젊은이들을 뽑으라는 것이었다. 그들은 왕의 집안이나 높은 집안 출신이어야 했다.

vi.L: Và vua bảo Át-bê-na, trưởng hoạn quan của mình, đem đến một số người trong con cái Y-sơ-ra-ên, cả thuộc dòng dõi hoàng tộc lẫn hàng quý tộc,
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua truyền cho Át-bê-na, quan đứng đầu các triều thần của vua, đem vào cung một số người Y-sơ-ra-ên thuộc dòng hoàng tộc và thuộc giới quý tộc,
vi.R: Vua ra lệnh cho Át-bê-na, viên quan đứng đầu cung điện. Vua bảo ông chọn một số thanh niên trong dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bị đem về Ba-by-lôn. Họ phải thuộc gia đình vua hoặc thuộc các gia đình quyền quý.

sw.L: Na mfalme akamwambia Ashpenazi, mkuu wa matowashi wake, alete baadhi ya wana wa Israeli, wa uzao wa kifalme na wa wakuu,
sw.B: Kisha mfalme akamwagiza Ashpenazi, mkuu wa maafisa wa ikulu yake, alete baadhi ya Waisraeli kutoka jamaa ya mfalme na kutoka familia za wakuu,
sw.R: Mfalme alimpa amri Ashpenazi, mkuu wa maafisa wa ikulu yake. Alimwambia achague baadhi ya vijana kutoka kwa watu wa Israeli waliokuwa wameletwa Babeli. Walipaswa kuwa wa jamaa ya mfalme na wa familia za watu wakuu.

decisions.choice: the chief of his eunuchs: the officer in charge of the palace staff
alternatives: the chief officer (without the sense of eunuch)
decisions.reason: The word *saris* can mean a castrated man and also, more generally, a royal officer, since many palace servants in the ancient Near East were eunuchs (Genesis 39:1 uses it of Potiphar, who had a wife). Isaiah warned Hezekiah that some of his descendants would be made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (Isaiah 39:7; 2 Kings 20:18). The text does not say whether Daniel and his friends were made eunuchs; it says only that they were put under this officer.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel ... the royal seed ... the nobles
decisions.reason: The young men are taken from the leading families of Judah: from the line of the kings and from the nobility. "Israel" here is the people as a whole. The word for "nobles" is a loanword from Persian, used only here and in Esther 1:3 and 6:9. Taking the sons of a conquered people's leaders to be trained at court was a known practice: it gave the empire officials and held the families to loyalty.

decisions.choice: eunuchs (L); court officer (B); palace officials (R)
decisions.reason: These follow the wording set for *saris* in Jeremiah: "eunuch" at Literal, "court officer" at Balanced and "palace official" at Readable (m1). Readable adds that the Israelites had been brought to Babylon, and makes "bring" a choice of young men, which verse 4 goes on to describe.

decisions.choice: Aspenaz; eunucos (L); funcionários da corte (B); oficiais do palácio (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the officer's name takes the Brazilian spelling "Aspenaz", and *saris* keeps the words Jeremiah (29:2; 38:7) and 2 Kings give it in Portuguese at each level (m1), so "o chefe dos eunucos" (L), "o chefe dos funcionários da corte" (B) and "o chefe dos oficiais do palácio" (R) through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "le chef des eunuques" (L), "le chef des hauts fonctionnaires" (B), "le chef des fonctionnaires du palais" (R), for the whole book
alternatives: "le chef des eunuques" at every level
decisions.reason: As the published French renders sarisim in Kings: the word could name a court official whether or not he was a eunuch, so Balanced and Readable name the office.

decisions.choice: "el jefe de sus eunucos" (L); "jefe de los funcionarios de su corte" (B); "el jefe de los funcionarios del palacio" (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide wording for rav sarisim, following the Kings choice of "eunucos" at L and "funcionarios" at B and R. "Aspenaz" spells the name as Spanish writes Hebrew sh

decisions.choice: "내시장" (L); "궁중 관리장" (B); "왕궁 관리들의 우두머리" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the chief of the eunuchs: Literal keeps the eunuch, Balanced and Readable give the office, as the English does; the same words hold through the chapter.

decisions.choice: trưởng hoạn quan (L); quan đứng đầu các triều thần (B); viên quan đứng đầu cung điện (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "eunuchs"; Balanced and Readable name the office, as the Kings note does ("hoạn quan / triều thần / quan chức"), since the meaning decision reads the title as the officer over the palace staff. These forms hold through the book.

decisions.choice: "mkuu wa matowashi" (L); "mkuu wa maafisa wa ikulu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Jeremiah 39:3: Literal keeps the word "towashi" (eunuch); Balanced and Readable name the office, the chief of the palace staff. Book-wide choice for Daniel.

decisions.choice: "Ashpenazi"
decisions.reason: A final vowel is added to the closed syllable, the usual Swahili pattern for a new name.

source.text: יְלָדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵֽין־בָּהֶ֣ם כָּל־מוּם֩ וְטוֹבֵ֨י מַרְאֶ֜ה וּמַשְׂכִּילִ֣ים בְּכָל־חָכְמָ֗ה וְיֹ֤דְעֵי דַ֨עַת֙ וּמְבִינֵ֣י מַדָּ֔ע וַאֲשֶׁר֙ כֹּ֣חַ בָּהֶ֔ם לַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּהֵיכַ֣ל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּֽלֲלַמְּדָ֥ם סֵ֖פֶר וּלְשׁ֥וֹן כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: youths who [was] not in them any blemish, and good of appearance, and having insight in all wisdom, and knowing knowledge, and understanding learning, and who [had] strength in them to stand in [the] palace of the king, and to teach them [the] writing and [the] language of [the] Chaldeans.

en.L: youths in whom [there was] no blemish, and good in appearance, and having insight in all wisdom, and knowing knowledge, and understanding learning, and who [had] ability in them to stand in the palace of the king, and to teach them the literature and the language of the Chaldeans.
en.B: young men without any defect, good-looking, skilled in every kind of wisdom, well informed and quick to learn, able to serve in the king's palace. He was to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
en.R: They were to be young men with no faults in their bodies, and good-looking. They were to be wise in every way, well educated, and quick to understand. They were to be fit to serve in the king's palace. Ashpenaz was to teach them to read and write the language of the Babylonians.

pt.L: jovens em quem não [havia] defeito algum, e de boa aparência, e entendidos em toda sabedoria, e conhecedores do conhecimento, e que compreendiam a ciência, e que [tinham] capacidade para estar no palácio do rei, e para lhes ensinar a literatura e a língua dos caldeus.
pt.B: jovens sem nenhum defeito, de boa aparência, preparados em todo tipo de sabedoria, bem informados e rápidos para aprender, capazes de servir no palácio do rei. Ele devia lhes ensinar a literatura e a língua dos caldeus.
pt.R: Deviam ser jovens sem nenhum defeito no corpo e bonitos. Deviam ser sábios em tudo, bem instruídos e rápidos para entender. Deviam ser capazes de servir no palácio do rei. Aspenaz devia ensinar a eles a ler e a escrever a língua dos babilônios.

fr.L: des jeunes gens en qui [il n’y avait] aucun défaut, et beaux d’apparence, et ayant de l’intelligence en toute sagesse, et connaissant la connaissance, et comprenant le savoir, et qui avaient en eux la capacité de se tenir dans le palais du roi, et pour leur enseigner l’écriture et la langue des Chaldéens.
fr.B: des jeunes gens sans aucun défaut, beaux, instruits en toute sagesse, bien informés et prompts à apprendre, capables de servir dans le palais du roi. Il devait leur enseigner la littérature et la langue des Chaldéens.
fr.R: Ils devaient être de jeunes hommes sans aucun défaut physique et beaux. Ils devaient être sages en toutes choses, bien instruits et rapides pour comprendre. Ils devaient être capables de servir dans le palais du roi. Ashpenaz devait leur apprendre à lire et à écrire la langue des Babyloniens.

es.L: jóvenes en quienes no [hubiera] ningún defecto, y de buen parecer, y entendidos en toda sabiduría, y conocedores de conocimiento, y capaces de entender la ciencia, y que [tuvieran] capacidad para estar en el palacio del rey, y para enseñarles las letras y la lengua de los caldeos.
es.B: jóvenes sin ningún defecto, bien parecidos, preparados en toda clase de sabiduría, bien instruidos y rápidos para aprender, aptos para servir en el palacio del rey. Aspenaz debía enseñarles la literatura y la lengua de los caldeos.
es.R: Tenían que ser jóvenes sin ningún defecto en el cuerpo y de buena apariencia. Debían ser sabios en todo, bien educados y rápidos para entender, y capaces de servir en el palacio del rey. Aspenaz tenía que enseñarles a leer y escribir la lengua de los babilonios.

ko.L: 그들은 흠이 없고 용모가 좋으며, 모든 지혜에 통찰력이 있고, 지식을 알며 학문을 깨닫고, 왕의 궁전에 설 능력이 있는 소년들이었고, [그는] 그들에게 갈대아 사람들의 문학과 언어를 가르쳐야 했다.
ko.B: 그들은 몸에 아무 흠이 없고 용모가 뛰어나며, 모든 분야의 지혜에 능하고, 지식이 풍부하고 배움이 빠르며, 왕궁에서 왕을 섬길 만한 젊은이들이어야 했다. 그는 그들에게 갈대아 사람들의 학문과 언어를 가르쳐야 했다.
ko.R: 그들은 몸에 아무 흠이 없고 잘생긴 젊은이들이어야 했다. 또 모든 면에서 지혜롭고, 많이 배웠고, 이해가 빨라야 했다. 그리고 왕궁에서 왕을 섬기기에 알맞은 사람들이어야 했다. 아스부나스는 그들에게 바빌로니아 사람들의 말과 글을 가르쳐야 했다.

vi.L: những thiếu niên không có tật nào, và đẹp về diện mạo, và thông sáng trong mọi sự khôn ngoan, và hiểu biết tri thức, và thông hiểu học vấn, và có năng lực để đứng chầu trong cung điện của vua, và để dạy cho họ văn chương và ngôn ngữ của người Canh-đê.
vi.B: là những thanh niên không có khuyết tật gì, đẹp đẽ, giỏi về mọi ngành khôn ngoan, hiểu biết rộng và học mau hiểu, đủ khả năng phục vụ trong cung vua. Ông phải dạy họ văn chương và ngôn ngữ của người Canh-đê.
vi.R: Họ phải là những thanh niên có thân thể không tì vết và đẹp trai. Họ phải khôn ngoan về mọi mặt, có học thức và mau hiểu. Họ phải đủ khả năng phục vụ trong cung vua. Át-bê-na phải dạy họ đọc, viết và nói tiếng của người Ba-by-lôn.

sw.L: vijana wasio na kasoro yoyote, na wazuri wa sura, na wenye ufahamu katika hekima yote, na wenye kujua maarifa, na wenye kuelewa elimu, na wenye uwezo wa kusimama katika jumba la mfalme, na kuwafundisha maandishi na lugha ya Wakaldayo.
sw.B: vijana wasio na kasoro yoyote mwilini, wenye sura nzuri, wenye ujuzi katika kila aina ya hekima, wenye maarifa na wepesi wa kujifunza, wenye uwezo wa kutumika katika jumba la mfalme. Alipaswa kuwafundisha maandishi na lugha ya Wakaldayo.
sw.R: Walipaswa kuwa vijana wasio na kasoro yoyote mwilini, tena wenye sura nzuri. Walipaswa kuwa na hekima ya kila namna, wenye elimu nzuri, na wepesi wa kuelewa. Walipaswa kufaa kutumika katika jumba la mfalme. Ashpenazi angewafundisha kusoma na kuandika lugha ya Wababeli.

decisions.choice: the literature and language of the Chaldeans: the learning of Babylon's scholars
decisions.reason: This is the written learning of Babylon: the cuneiform script, the old languages in which it was written, and the large body of texts on omens, dreams, astronomy, medicine and law that the court's experts used. Here the Chaldeans are the people of Babylon; later in the book the same word names a class of these experts (2:2).

decisions.choice: having insight ... knowing knowledge ... understanding learning: able and quick to learn
decisions.reason: The three phrases pile up words for wisdom and knowledge to describe young men with every gift for study. The point is their ability to learn, which the next verses test; the same words return when God gives them knowledge and insight (verse 17).

decisions.choice: to stand in the king's palace: to serve the king
decisions.reason: To "stand before" or "in the palace of" a king is to serve as one of his officials, ready for his orders (verse 5; 1 Kings 10:8).

decisions.choice: He was to teach them (B); Ashpenaz was to teach them (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs on from verse 3 in one sentence, with the teaching as the last thing the king ordered. Balanced and Readable start a new sentence for it, and Readable names Ashpenaz. Readable says "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans as a people, as the book's table sets, and "read and write" for "the writing".

decisions.choice: os caldeus (L, B); os babilônios (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the people and their learning are meant (m1): "os caldeus" at Literal and Balanced and "os babilônios" at Readable, as Jeremiah has them in Portuguese and as the English Readable says "Babylonians". Where the word names the class of court experts (2:2 and after), it is "os caldeus" at Literal and Balanced and "os astrólogos" at Readable, as the English has "Chaldeans" and "astrologers".

decisions.choice: "les Chaldéens" (Literal, Balanced), "les Babyloniens" (Readable), for the whole book; for the class of experts (from 2:2) "les astrologues" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the term sheet for these books and the published Jeremiah: Readable names the people plainly; where Daniel means the scholars of Babylon, Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: "los caldeos" (L, B); "los babilonios" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the Chaldeans are the people whose language is taught, so R says "los babilonios"; where they are a class of experts (2:2 and later) R says "los astrólogos"

decisions.choice: "갈대아 사람들의 문학과 언어" (L); "학문과 언어" (B); "바빌로니아 사람들의 말과 글" (R)
decisions.reason: Chaldeans as a people are "갈대아 사람들" (L, B) and "바빌로니아 사람들" (R), as in the published Jeremiah; Balanced says "학문" because the meaning decision reads the phrase as the learning of Babylon's scholars.

decisions.choice: người Canh-đê (L, B); người Ba-by-lôn (R)
decisions.reason: Kasdim here is the people whose learning and language the young men study. Literal and Balanced keep "người Canh-đê", as Kings and Jeremiah do; Readable says "người Ba-by-lôn". Where the word names the class of experts (2:2 on), Readable says "các nhà chiêm tinh".

decisions.choice: "Wakaldayo" (L, B); "Wababeli" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 24-25 and Jeremiah: Readable names the people by their city. Book-wide choice for Daniel; where Chaldeans are a class of experts (2:2) Readable says "wanajimu".

source.text: וַיְמַן֩ לָהֶ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֗וֹ מִפַּת־בַּ֤ג הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וּמִיֵּ֣ין מִשְׁתָּ֔יו וּֽלְגַדְּלָ֖ם שָׁנִ֣ים שָׁל֑וֹשׁ וּמִ֨קְצָתָ֔ם יַֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And assigned to them the king [the] matter of a day in its day from [the] delicacies of the king and from [the] wine of his drinking, and to bring them up years three, and at [the] end of them they would stand before the king.

en.L: And the king assigned them a daily portion from the king's delicacies and from the wine that he drank, and [ordered them] to be educated three years, and at the end of them they were to stand before the king.
en.B: The king assigned them a daily ration from the royal food and from the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, and after that they were to enter the king's service.
en.R: The king ordered that they be given food and wine every day from his own table. They were to be trained for three years. After that they would begin to serve the king.

pt.L: E o rei lhes designou uma porção diária das iguarias do rei e do vinho que ele bebia, e [ordenou] que fossem educados três anos, e ao fim deles estariam diante do rei.
pt.B: O rei lhes designou uma ração diária da comida real e do vinho que ele bebia. Eles deviam ser preparados durante três anos e, depois disso, entrariam no serviço do rei.
pt.R: O rei mandou que eles recebessem todos os dias comida e vinho da sua própria mesa. Eles deviam ser treinados durante três anos. Depois disso, começariam a servir o rei.

fr.L: Et le roi leur assigna la portion de chaque jour sur ses mets royaux et sur le vin qu’il buvait, et [ordonna] de les instruire trois ans, et au bout de ce [temps] ils se tiendraient devant le roi.
fr.B: Le roi leur attribua une ration quotidienne des mets royaux et du vin qu’il buvait. Ils devaient être formés pendant trois ans, puis entrer au service du roi.
fr.R: Le roi a ordonné qu’on leur donne chaque jour de la nourriture et du vin de sa propre table. Ils devaient être formés pendant trois ans. Après cela, ils commenceraient à servir le roi.

es.L: Y el rey les asignó una porción diaria de los manjares del rey y del vino que él bebía, y [mandó] que los educaran tres años, y que al cabo de ellos se presentaran delante del rey.
es.B: El rey les asignó una ración diaria de la comida real y del vino que él bebía. Debían ser preparados durante tres años, y después entrarían al servicio del rey.
es.R: El rey ordenó que cada día les dieran comida y vino de su propia mesa. Iban a recibir instrucción durante tres años, y después empezarían a servir al rey.

ko.L: 그리고 왕은 그들에게 왕의 진미와 그가 마시는 포도주 가운데서 날마다 그날의 몫을 정해 주었고, 그들을 삼 년 동안 기르게 [했으며], 그 끝에 그들은 왕 앞에 서게 되어 있었다.
ko.B: 왕은 자기가 먹는 음식과 자기가 마시는 포도주 가운데서 날마다 그들의 몫을 정해 주었다. 그들은 삼 년 동안 교육을 받은 뒤에 왕을 섬기게 되어 있었다.
ko.R: 왕은 자기 식탁에 오르는 음식과 포도주를 날마다 그들에게 주라고 명령했다. 그들은 삼 년 동안 훈련을 받아야 했다. 그 뒤에 왕을 섬기기 시작할 것이었다.

vi.L: Và vua cấp cho họ phần ăn mỗi ngày từ cao lương mỹ vị của vua và từ rượu vua uống, và [truyền] nuôi dạy họ ba năm, và cuối [thời gian] ấy họ sẽ đứng chầu trước mặt vua.
vi.B: Vua định cho họ khẩu phần hằng ngày lấy từ thức ăn của hoàng gia và rượu vua uống. Họ phải được huấn luyện trong ba năm, rồi sau đó sẽ vào phục vụ vua.
vi.R: Vua ra lệnh cho họ ăn uống mỗi ngày bằng thức ăn và rượu từ bàn ăn của chính vua. Họ phải được huấn luyện trong ba năm. Sau đó họ sẽ bắt đầu phục vụ vua.

sw.L: Na mfalme akawapangia posho ya kila siku kutoka vyakula vitamu vya mfalme na kutoka divai aliyokunywa, na [akaagiza] waelimishwe miaka mitatu, na mwisho wake wasimame mbele ya mfalme.
sw.B: Mfalme akawapangia posho ya kila siku kutoka vyakula vya kifalme na kutoka divai aliyokunywa. Walipaswa kufunzwa kwa miaka mitatu, na baada ya hapo waingie katika utumishi wa mfalme.
sw.R: Mfalme aliagiza wapewe chakula na divai kila siku kutoka mezani pake mwenyewe. Walipaswa kufunzwa kwa miaka mitatu. Baada ya hapo wangeanza kumtumikia mfalme.

decisions.choice: the king's delicacies: the food provided from the royal table
decisions.reason: The word is a loanword from Persian, used only in Daniel (1:5, 8, 13, 15, 16; 11:26). It means the portion of food a king assigned to those who ate at his expense, perhaps the best of it. The young men were fed as members of the court.

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: a daily allowance
decisions.reason: The phrase is the Hebrew way of saying "each day's portion on its day" (compare 2 Kings 25:30, of the allowance given to King Jehoiachin in Babylon).

decisions.choice: they would stand before the king: they would enter his service
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, to stand before the king is to serve him. The three years of training ended in an examination by the king himself (verses 18-20).

decisions.choice: trained (B, R); educated (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring up or raise, as a child is raised. Literal says "educated", with "ordered them" in brackets, since the king's order carries over from the start of the verse; Balanced and Readable say "trained".

decisions.choice: as iguarias do rei (L); a comida real (B); a comida do rei (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter (verses 8, 13, 15, 16): "iguarias" at Literal for the fine food of the king's table (m1); "manjares" is literary and old. Balanced and Readable say plainly what it was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "왕 앞에 서게" (L); "왕을 섬기게" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable give its sense, entering the king's service, as the meaning decision reads it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה דָּנִיֵּ֣אל חֲנַנְיָ֔ה מִֽישָׁאֵ֖ל וַעֲזַרְיָֽה׃

en.R: Four of these young men were from the tribe of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

es.R: Cuatro de estos jóvenes eran de la tribu de Judá: Daniel, Hananías, Misael y Azarías.

ko.L: 그리고 그들 가운데 유다 자손 중에서는 다니엘, 하나냐, 미사엘, 아사랴가 있었다.
